newsitem.title: UK: UK govt's chance of surviving censure vote rise.
newsitem.headline: UK govt's chance of surviving censure vote rise.

text.p: The British government's chances of surviving a censure motion against its agriculture minister improved on Saturday when a member of a Northern Irish party said he expected his colleagues to be present for the vote.
The Ulster Unionist parties can usually be relied on to support the ruling Conservative Party, which could face a no-confidence vote if the censure motion is passed on Monday.
The opposition Labour Party has called the motion, effectively seeking Douglas Hogg's resignation over his handling of the mad cow crisis, which has crushed Britain's beef export market.

Prime Minister John Major told parliament last week that the export ban imposed over fears of bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE or mad cow disease) in British cattle had cost the country 3.3 billion pounds ($5.4 billion).
Ulster Unionist Party member Ken Maginnis said he expected most of the nine members of parliament from his party to be present for Monday's vote.
"I expect that everybody who is able to adjust, as I myself have had to adjust, his diary will be there," he told British television.
Last week, the UUP's whip, Martin Smyth, who is responsible for getting his party's MPs to attend votes, called the motion "bogus" and said he would not be in parliament on Monday.
Major no longer has a majority in parliament and relies heavily on the Ulster parties to keep him in power.
He must hold an election by May 22 and is believed to be holding out until the last moment in the hope of narrowing Labour's 20 point opinion poll lead before setting a polling date.
